summary: High tail latency and intermittent timeouts when using structured JSON output mode
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in tail latency (95th/99th) and sporadic request timeouts for requests that request structured JSON output (content-mode: json / structured output settings). The error pattern started after a model rollout on 2026-03-09 and affects a subset of long-completion prompts where the model is instructed to return nested JSON objects or arrays.

Impact:
- Several production endpoints for DataWeave ingest pipelines are experiencing 5–10% request timeouts and 95th/99th token latency spikes (up to 8s per token) when using structured output mode.
- Customer batch job throughput dropped by ~30% and they hit their SLOs for downstream consumers.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod) in us-east region
- Model variants: redwood/gpt-4o-mini-structured-v1 (primary), fallback to llama2-70b-instruct observed
- Requests use streaming=true + content_mode=structured_json flag set in request metadata

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) POST /v1/generate with the schema prompt (attached) asking for nested order objects (~500 tokens expected).
2) Set streaming=true and response_format=json (structured mode).
3) Observe first tokens stream normally but 95th+ percentile tokens stall or occasionally connection times out after 10s.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming tokens arrive evenly paced, no extreme tail latency, no request timeouts for valid structured outputs.

Actual behavior:
- Long tail latency for final JSON closing tokens. Some requests fully timeout; partial JSON is sometimes returned with truncated payloads.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- example_prompt.txt (attached in ticket), request_id samples: rw-req-20260310-2217-017, rw-req-20260310-2209-591
- pcap of client connection (sensitive) shared privately with Support via SFTP link

Initial troubleshooting performed by customer:
- Disabled structured mode (falling back to plain text) and latency returned to baseline.
- Reduced max_output_tokens to 150 and timeouts stopped (suggests problem scales with long structured outputs).

Notes on security/privacy: customer sent redacted dataset samples. No PII in attachments per customer verification.

investigation_notes: Repro in staging: use same prompt + model variant; with structured mode enabled, decode_worker queue length grows linearly with token count beyond ~300 tokens.
Heap/GC: decode worker processes show increased GC pause times under structured-mode workloads; likely due to full-object JSON validation and buffer copies.
Telemetry: tokenization and kernel runtimes unaffected; CPU waiting appears in Golang sidecar responsible for output post-processing.
Hypothesis: structured output path performs a synchronous JSON schema validation/finalization step that blocks streamer goroutines until end-of-output, producing long tail latency on long outputs.
Experiment: patch runtime to perform incremental validation and stream validated chunks instead of waiting for final framing (PR #1392). Canary shows improvement; will monitor memory usage.
Related: linked INT-412 reported a similar symptom internally during a model experiment; cross-referencing their heap dumps was useful.
resolution:
Partial mitigation applied: customer advised to set content_mode=plain_text or disable structured JSON streaming as an immediate workaround. Canary runtime change (PR #1392) deployed to 3% traffic in us-east; metrics show 99th token latency improvement. Next steps: widen canary to 20% then 100% pending QA.

Planned permanent fix steps:
- Merge incremental validation change after perf testing and memory analysis.
- Add server-side telemetry that emits structured-mode decode queue length and per-request JSON-finalization time to help future debugging.
- Backfill regression test that simulates long nested JSON streaming to catch regressions in CI.

Customer follow-up: Engineering to provide ETA for full rollout by 2026-03-20 and schedule a post-deployment validation call.
